question_text: What would happen to a buck converter if you completely removed the Output Capacitor?
answer_text: The load would experience massive voltage ripple, turning the output into a jagged waveform instead of DC.
explanation_text: The inductor provides a choppy, triangular current. Without the output capacitor to act as a "bucket"—absorbing the excess current peaks and filling in the valleys—the load would see that raw, changing current, resulting in massive voltage swings. You should really build this on LTspice to see it in action. An LTspice model will be added in the future if deemed necessary.
